callbacks.notes: Upstream and Rust both filter the cop by Include/Exclude before running one on_new_investigation callback over the complete processed source. The compatibility scheduler supplies the shared Parser-shaped AST once and retains no cop state between files.

restrictions.notes: Both return for blank input and select every implicit-receiver send named group from the complete AST. Rust's relevant_file fallback restores RuboCop's built-in Gemfile/gems.rb/*.gemfile defaults only when resolved Include metadata is absent.

configuration.notes: The cop has no bespoke settings beyond Include and Severity. RuboCop applies Include before investigation; Rust applies resolved path policy before scheduling and effective severity while registering diagnostics.

lifecycle_state.notes: Both implementations allocate ordered duplicate buckets within one investigation and retain no cross-file state.

helpers.notes: Rust mirrors the upstream decomposition into group_declarations, duplicated_group_nodes, find_source_key, group_attributes, and register_offense. Shared adapters provide Parser-shaped traversal, arbitrary-precision Ruby numeric value.to_s, exact binary source bytes, and RangeHelp.

predicates.notes: Both distinguish hash arguments from scalar/source arguments, sort pair source strings, use unbounded Ruby value.to_s semantics for Parser literals, and restrict source context to the nearest source, git, platforms, or path block.

traversal.notes: Both search the complete AST in encounter order and follow real block ancestors; multiline calls, nested expressions, ordinary blocks, and explicit receivers therefore use the same topology rather than a textual approximation.

offenses.notes: Both report every duplicate after the first, preserve the duplicate node's exact argument source bytes in the message, and construct the location from the send's first-line column through last_column, including descending multiline ranges.

corrections.notes: The upstream cop registers offenses without a corrector and Rust likewise emits non-correctable diagnostics.

mixins.notes: Upstream RangeHelp#source_range and Rust RangeHelp::source_range_columns both translate the one-based line and character-column range through the processed source buffer.

correspondences.invariant: The cop receives exactly one complete processed source per selected, successfully parsed file and retains no cross-file state.
All grouping state is allocated and discarded within one investigation.
Encounter-ordered declarations are bucketed by the same composite key and only buckets with more than one declaration survive.
Every implicit-receiver group send is discovered once in Parser/RuboCop AST encounter order.
The nearest recognized source, git, platforms, or path block ancestor supplies the same method and first-argument source key.
Hash arguments are represented by their pair source strings sorted and joined exactly as upstream.
Attributes compare byte-exact Ruby literal value.to_s identity, including delimiter-independent dynamic and command strings, invalid string bytes, and equivalent unbounded numeric values.
The duplicate argument interpolation preserves the exact decoded-or-binary source bytes RuboCop places in its message.
Every duplicate after the first must use the exact argument-source message, first occurrence line, severity, and Parser character range.
Offense geometry is derived from the send node's first line, column, and last column through SourceBuffer character positions.
The callback is scheduled and its findings retained only for paths selected by the same configured or built-in Include and Exclude patterns.
Every duplicate finding carries the same configured or fallback severity RuboCop resolves while adding the offense.
